Fourth version of the Hexagon preprint https://hexagonmath.org/2610.00471v3 (amsart, single column, 36 pages). It supersedes the package of release v2.0.0.

Four results are new, and together they make the Main Theorem a classification. Theorem 5.12 (Section 5.5) shows that the conditions of the Main Theorem are sufficient when the residual dimension is ten: a complex isometry that keeps the total dimension and the rank of the null frame carries Nishino's equations to every signature with s+t-2k = 10 and s-t in {8, 0, -8}, and the transported theory keeps a Majorana-Weyl gaugino and satisfies N1-N5; by Corollary 5.13 theories exist in 9+9 and 9+17, the members n = 1, 2 of the second degenerate family 9+(1+8n) of Rios, Marrani and Chester, and in no member with n >= 3. Theorem 5.14 (Section 5.6) settles residual dimension two: in every signature (k+1)+(k+1), Nishino's transformations written with a real frame of rank k satisfy N1-N5, the cubic gaugino terms vanish identically, and the supersymmetry algebra closes off shell on translations along one null direction of the residual plane; for k = 0 this is two-dimensional super Yang-Mills theory with one Majorana-Weyl supercharge. Corollary 5.15 states the classification: a theory of rank k exists if and only if s+t-2k = 10 and s-t in {8, 0, -8}, or s+t-2k = 2 and s = t. Theorem 7.3 (Section 7.2) drops N4 and allows any fixed tensor u in the source J ^ u that absorbs the cubic gaugino terms, with or without a constraint on the gaugino: the residual dimension is then at most 14, and at most 10 unless the frame has rank at least 54, so by Corollary 7.4 no contraction of the source rescues the families (9+8n)+1, (10+8n)+2, (11+8n)+3, (12+8n)+4 with n >= 1; this covers the spacelike contraction that v3 left open in a footnote. Proposition 7.5 (Section 7.3) treats several gauginos that each transform with their own parameter, as in extended supersymmetry: for every residual dimension of at least three the cubic terms that couple two gauginos cannot vanish, by an irreducibility argument for the vector representation. Remark 7.6 explains why no statement about the superalgebra alone can exclude every theory: the superalgebra acts on superfields with tensorial coordinates. Theories with auxiliary fields, nonlinear transformation rules, gauginos mixed by their transformation rules or a non-Lie gauge structure remain outside the results. Appendices E and F check the new results in explicit gamma matrices (`verification/code/contraction_check.py`, 32 checks; `verification/code/residual_two_check.py`, 50 checks; logs in `verification/current/`); Figures 7 and 11 are drawn by `verification/code/figures/make_v4_figures.py`. The abstract was rewritten to state the classification. The citations of unrefereed preprints were removed: the arXiv paper of Truini, Marrani and Rios is replaced by its published version (Expo. Math. 43 (2025) 125621, with de Graaf), the arXiv preprint of Banerjee and two self-archived Zenodo copies of earlier versions are no longer cited, and the data availability section cites one concept record. The introduction, Section 7.4 (Scope), Remark 7.7, the conclusions and the proof map were updated, the second affiliation now names Heramba Chandra College, and a typo in Appendix A was fixed. Sections 2-4 and 6, Proposition 7.1, Remark 7.2 and Appendices B-D are unchanged; in Section 5 the paragraph on existence after Corollary 5.9 was replaced by Sections 5.5 and 5.6.

Files: `NullProjectedSYM_v4-tex.zip` (the source to upload; main.tex, pdfLaTeX; the Python programs in `anc/`), `NullProjectedSYM_v4.pdf`, `NullProjectedSYM_v4-arxiv.tar.gz`, `HEXAGON_FORM.md` and `AI_PROVENANCE.md`. The source compiles with `pdflatex -jobname=output main.tex` with no errors, no bad boxes and no undefined references. `scripts/verify.py` (34 checks), `transfer_check.py` (24 checks), `contraction_check.py` (32 checks) and `residual_two_check.py` (50 checks) pass.
